Frame, for paragraph text: the background color of the frame, the vertical alignment (top, middle, bottom), fit text to frame, columns (1 to 8) and the gap between them, and links to the bullets, drop cap and columns dialog boxes, and hyphenation. Every change applies to the selected characters while editing, or to the selected texts, and is one undo step. With no text selected, the settings become those of new text. The button at the top right gives new text the settings of the selected text. Paragraph text frames Frames show as dashed lines. A frame turns red, with a small tab under its bottom edge, when its text does not fit; the text that does not fit is not drawn, printed or exported. To make it fit: drag the frame's handles to enlarge it. The text flows again; the letters keep their size; choose Text > Paragraph Text Frame > Fit Text to Frame to resize the text to fill the frame; link the frame to another one, so the text flows on: Link. Unlink breaks the link. Or click the small tab under the frame's bottom edge, then click another frame (on this page or another one) or click or drag on an empty spot for a new frame: the text flows on into it. Text > Show Text Frames shows or hides the frames. Moving and turning characters With the Shape tool, text shows a node at each character: drag nodes to move characters, and drag the arrows at the corners of the text to change the character, word and line spacing. The character offsets and angle can also be typed in the Text panel. Text > Straighten Text puts characters back in line, and Align to Baseline (Alt+F12) removes their vertical offsets. Text on a path Select a text and a curve or shape. Choose Text > Fit Text to Path. Or click the outline of a path with the Text tool and type. Text on a closed shape stands on its outside, centered on its top. With text on a path selected, the property bar sets the orientation of the letters (rotated, vertical or horizontal skew, or upright), the vertical placement (on the baseline, ascender, descender or center), the placement along the path, the distance and offset, and mirroring. Drag the text to slide it along the path. Straighten Text takes it off the path. Other text commands Text > Insert Formatting Code: special characters such as Em Space, Non-breaking Space, Optional Hyphen and Column/Frame Break. Show Non-Printing Characters shows spaces, tabs and breaks. Make Text Web-compatible prepares text for web pages. Text > Convert switches between artistic and paragraph text. Converting text to curves (Object > Convert to Curves) keeps its look without the font. Text files can be imported; see Importing files.

t: Tabs, columns, bullets and drop caps
h: Tabs Columns Bullets Drop caps Hyphenation
x: Tabs, columns, bullets and drop caps The Text menu has four dialog boxes for laying out paragraph text. Each acts on the selected paragraph text. Their settings are also in the Frame section of the Text panel. Tabs Text > Tabs sets where the Tab character jumps to. At first there is a tab stop every 12.7 mm (half an inch). Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Tabs. Under Tab stops, change the positions, or click Add tab to add one. Click Close.  Columns Text > Columns splits a text frame into columns; the text flows from one column into the next. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Columns. Set the number of Columns and the Gutter, the space between columns (5 mm at first). Click Close.  To break to the next column at a given place, insert Column/Frame Break from Insert Formatting Code. Bullets Text > Bullets puts a bullet before each paragraph. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Bullets. Tick Use bullets, and set the bullet Symbol and the Indent (5 mm at first). Click Close.  Drop caps A drop cap is a large first letter that spans several lines. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Drop Cap. Tick Use drop cap and set the Lines dropped (3 at first). Click Close. The letter is scaled so its top meets the top of the first line and it sits on the baseline of the last line it spans; the lines beside it are shortened to make room.  Hyphenation Text > Use Hyphenation lets the selected text's words break at the end of lines (while you type in a text, the paragraphs at the cursor; with no text selected, it is the setting for new text), with at least two letters before and three after the break. A comma or other punctuation next to a word does not stop it from breaking, and words with an apostrophe (such as Italian dell'anno) break too. Words with a capital letter are never broken. To decide yourself where a word may break, see Custom hyphens.

h: The Fonts panel Missing fonts The Font Sampler The Glyphs panel The Font Manager
x: Fonts and glyphs TraceDraw uses the fonts installed on your computer, fonts you add in the Font Manager, and fonts that come with a drawing. This page explains the panels and the dialog box for working with fonts and special characters. The Fonts panel The Fonts panel lists the font families.  Type in the filter field to narrow the list. Under Fonts in document are the families the drawing uses. A family that is not installed is marked missing; its text shows in a similar font and keeps its font name. A family that came with the drawing is marked embedded. Click a family to give it to the selected text, or to make it the font of new text. Missing fonts When a drawing uses fonts that are not installed, a message names them after it opens (see Notes after opening). Install the fonts and the text shows in them again. Drawings saved as .tdraw, and .cdr files with embedded fonts, can carry their fonts along. The Font Sampler The Font Sampler panel (Text > Font Sampler) shows a line of sample text in several fonts, one under the other, to compare them.  Type the sample text at the top; left empty, a sentence in your interface language is used. Set the size (10 to 96, 28 at first). Add fonts by typing part of a name and clicking one of the matches (up to 24 fonts); the cross removes one. At first the panel lists the text font and the fonts of the drawing. Click a sample to give that font to the selected text. The Glyphs panel The Glyphs panel (Text > Glyphs, Ctrl+F11) shows every character of a font, to insert symbols and special characters.  Choose the font. Choose a character range: the entire font, Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, punctuation, numbers, currency, arrows, mathematical operators or symbols. Click a character. It is inserted at the caret of the text you are editing, or as a new text in the middle of the page. Hover a character to see its name and code. A small arrow under a character means the font has alternates for it (such as swashes or small capitals); click it to see them. The glyphs you used last are at the top of the panel. Type in the search field above the grid to find characters: type the characters themselves (such as é), or a Unicode code point such as U+20AC, 0x20ac or 20AC. The line above the grid shows the code point, the character and the range of the character under the pointer. The Font Manager Tools > Font Manager opens the Font Manager, a window that organizes your fonts.  Libraries (top left): My fonts (the installed fonts), the folders you added, Favorites and your collections. Double-click a collection to rename it; right-click for more. Filters (bottom left): by status (installed, not installed, protected system fonts, duplicates), embedding rights, technology (TrueType, OpenType, variable), weight, width, style, character range and OpenType features. Clear removes them. Right side: the sample text and its presets, a search field (family, style or PostScript name), and the fonts as cards, grouped by family. Each card shows a sample, the technology and a bar that is green when the font is installed. Click to pick a font, Ctrl+click to pick several. To use the Font Manager: Add folder scans a folder for font files (TTF, OTF, TTC, OTC); its fonts show as not installed. Add font installs one file at once. Install makes the picked fonts available in TraceDraw, now and at every start. Uninstall removes them; the system's own fonts are protected. Add to collection and Remove from collection organize fonts; drag fonts onto Favorites or a collection to add them. Double-click an installed font, or choose Use in drawing, to give it to the selected text. Show details shows the family, style, version, file, technology, embedding rights, weight, width, glyph count, scripts and features of the font you clicked. Fonts the drawing uses that are not installed are listed in orange above the cards. In the browser version, Add font loads a font file for the session only.

h: The Writing Tools dialog box Spell Checker Dictionaries Grammar Thesaurus Autocorrect Custom hyphens Change case Text statistics Encode Web-compatible text
x: Writing tools TraceDraw checks spelling and grammar, finds synonyms, corrects as you type, and fixes text that came in with the wrong characters. The commands are in Text > Writing Tools and the Text menu. The Writing Tools dialog box Text > Writing Tools > Spell Check, Grammar and Thesaurus open the Writing Tools dialog box at that tab. Check chooses whether to check every text of the page (Document) or only the selected texts (Selection).  Spell Checker Click Start. The first word not found shows, with suggestions under Replacements. Click a suggestion to put it in Replace with (double-click to replace at once), or type the right word. Click Replace for this place, Auto Replace for every place, Skip Once or Skip All to leave it, or Add to add the word to your own word list. Undo takes back the last replacement. Options has Ignore words with numbers, Ignore words in capitals and Add corrections to Autocorrect. Dictionaries TraceDraw checks spelling with Hunspell dictionaries: for each language a .dic file and an .aff file with the same name, such as pt_BR.dic and pt_BR.aff. Free dictionaries for most languages can be downloaded from the projects that make them; other programs often install them too. Open Tools > Options > Text > Spelling. Click Open Folder and copy the .dic and .aff files into that folder (folders inside it work too), or name a folder that already has dictionaries in Also read dictionaries from. Click Read Again. The Dictionaries list shows each one; clear a box to stop using it. A word is right when any dictionary in use knows it. Dictionaries installed on your system are used as well. Without any, only a built-in word list is used. Hyphenation dictionaries (hyph_ files such as hyph_pt_BR.dic) go in the same folders. Choose one under Text > Paragraph Text > Hyphenation patterns to hyphenate text in that language. Grammar The grammar checker finds doubled words, double spaces, spaces before punctuation, missing spaces after it, sentences that start in lower case, unbalanced brackets and quotes, repeated punctuation, sentences over 40 words, missing end marks and, in English, "a" and "an" before the wrong sound. For each finding it shows the replacement, the New sentence and the Rule Name. Click Start (then Replace), Skip Once or Skip Rule. Thesaurus Type a word (the first word of the selected text at first) and click Look Up. The meanings show with their synonyms: click one to pick it, double-click to look it up. Insert puts it in the text, keeping the capitals. Under Options, Close after inserting closes the dialog box after inserting, and Choose Thesaurus File uses a thesaurus file you have. Autocorrect Text > Writing Tools > Autocorrect opens the Autocorrect tab of Tools > Options > Text, which sets what is corrected while you type: Capitalize first letter of sentences; Correct two initial capitals ("THe" becomes "The"); Capitalize names of days ("monday" becomes "Monday"); Automatically create hyperlinks when typing web addresses: typing www.example.com or an address starting with http:// or https:// gives the text object that hyperlink, unless it has one; Language the language whose quotation marks are used (the interface language unless you pick another); Use typographic quotation marks, and Use straight quotation marks after numbers (e.g. 6'); Single quotes and Double quotes: the Open and Close marks, if you want others than the language's; the Replacement table, used when Replace text while typing is on: (c) becomes ©, (r) ®, (tm) ™, 1/2 ½ and so on. Type in Replace and With, then click Add; click a row to Delete it, or change its text and click Replace. Apply to Selection applies the rules to the selected text. Text you paste or import is never changed.  Custom hyphens Text > Custom Optional Hyphens (also the gear of the Paragraph section of the Text panel) defines where your own words may break, such as product names. Those words break only there when hyphenation is on. Choose the Language (Show all languages lists every one). Type the Word and the Hyphenated Word with hyphens where it may break, such as Trace-Draw. Click Add Definition. Remove Definition removes the selected definition. Under Automatically insert custom optional hyphens, When typing and When pasting and importing text turn hyphenation on for texts that hold a defined word. Click Apply to Selection to apply them to the selected text now, or OK to keep them.  Change case Text > Change Case changes the selected text to Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title Case or tOGGLE cASE.  Text statistics Text > Text Statistics counts the text objects, lines, words, characters and fonts of the selected text, or of the page.  Encode Text that came from another program sometimes shows the wrong characters, such as "cafÃ©" instead of "café". Text > Encode fixes it: Select the text. Choose how the text Text was read as and what It really is (UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1, Mac OS Roman or Windows-1251). Check the Preview and click OK.  Web-compatible text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies the selected text for web pages: gradient, pattern, texture and mesh fills become a flat color, and outlines, shadows and effects are removed.

Plantillas y estilos Las plantillas y los estilos ahorran trabajo que de otro modo repetiría. Una plantilla es un dibujo preparado del que partir. Un estilo es un conjunto con nombre de relleno, contorno y transparencia que sigue vinculado a los objetos que lo usan, de modo que un cambio los actualiza a todos. Las propiedades predeterminadas deciden el aspecto de los objetos nuevos. Los estilos de color, que funcionan igual para colores sueltos, se explican en Estilos de color.

h: Starting from a template The built-in templates Saving your own templates
x: Templates A template is a drawing to start from: a blank page of a common size, or a designed business card, flyer, poster, letterhead or label to fill in. Opening a template makes a new, untitled drawing; the template itself never changes. Starting from a template Choose File > New from Template, or click New from Template on the Welcome Screen. Find a template: type in Search templates to match names and categories; choose where templates come from: All templates, Built in or My templates; choose a category, or All categories. Click a template to see it. With Show template details on, the pane on the right shows it large with its Category, Page size and Source. Click Open, double-click the template, or press Enter. The Size slider at the bottom makes the thumbnails larger or smaller, and Open template opens any .tdt or .tdraw file as a template.  The built-in templates Blank pages: A4 portrait and landscape, A3, Letter, business card (90 by 50 mm), A2 poster, web (1920 by 1080 pixels) and social media (1080 by 1080 pixels). Designed: two business cards, a sale flyer and an event flyer, a poster, a letterhead, a certificate, an invoice, a birthday banner, a quote post and a round label. They are made of ordinary shapes and text with sample text, so you can change every part. Saving your own templates Make the drawing you want to start from in the future. Choose File > Save as Template. Give it a name and save it. Templates you save appear under My templates. They are kept in the templates folder of your settings, so they are not available in the browser version.

h: Default properties Changing defaults with nothing selected Styles To make a style Using and changing styles
x: Object styles and default properties The Object Styles panel has two parts: the Default Properties of new objects, and the styles of the drawing. Both are saved with the drawing. Open it from Window > Panels, or right-click an object and choose the object styles panel.  Default properties New objects take the fill and outline of their kind: Graphic: shapes, lines, tables and everything except text no fill, a thin black outline Artistic text: text without a frame black fill, no outline Paragraph text: text in a frame black fill, no outline In the panel, each kind shows its fill and outline, with From Selection (take the fill and outline of the selected object) and Reset (back to the defaults of a new drawing). Changing defaults with nothing selected When nothing is selected and you choose a fill or outline (click a palette color, use a fill tool, change the outline color or width), the change goes to new objects. TraceDraw asks which kinds of new objects it applies to: Tick Graphic, Artistic text and Paragraph text as needed. The kinds you ticked last time are ticked. Tick Use these kinds from now on without asking to skip the question from now on. Click OK. Cancel changes nothing.  The check box Ask which kinds a change with nothing selected applies to in the panel turns the question on or off. The Properties panel with nothing selected also edits the Graphic defaults. To keep the defaults for every new drawing, choose Tools > Save Settings as Default. Styles A style is a named set of properties: Fill, Outline (its color, width, line style and arrowheads) and Transparency. Objects you give a style stay linked to it: change the style and they all change. To make a style Select an object with the look you want. Click New style from selection. The style is named "Style 1" and so on, takes the fill, outline and transparency of the object, and is linked to every selected object. Using and changing styles Each style shows its swatches, its name (click it to rename), how many objects are linked to it, and its parts as check boxes: Apply gives the selection the style and links it. Update from selection takes the fill, outline and transparency of the selected object; every linked object follows. Turning a part off leaves that property to each object. Delete removes the style; linked objects keep their look. Break Link to Style unlinks the selected objects, which keep their look. You can still change a linked object directly; the next change of its style sets the style's parts again. Right-click an object to apply a style from its menu.

Páginas y diseño Un dibujo puede tener muchas páginas, cada una con su tamaño y orientación. Estas páginas explican cómo añadir, ordenar y numerar páginas, definir las opciones del documento (tamaño de página, diseño, fondo, sangrado, reglas, cuadrícula y líneas guía), colocar líneas guía, ajustar objetos a su sitio y leer las propiedades de un dibujo.

h: Moving between pages The Pages panel Inserting pages Deleting pages Duplicating a page Renaming a page Page size and orientation Page numbers Page background
x: Working with pages Moving between pages Click a page tab under the drawing window, or use the page navigator beside them (first, previous, next and last page). Press PgUp or PgDn. Choose Layout > Go to Page, type the page number in the Go To Page dialog box and click OK.  The Pages panel The Pages panel lists the pages of the drawing. Click a page to go to it. Its buttons Insert Page, Delete Page and Duplicate Page act on the current page, and Page Sorter View shows every page as a thumbnail. Open it from Window > Panels.  Inserting pages Choose Layout > Insert Page, or click one of the insert buttons of the page navigator (they add one page of the current size before or after the current page at once). In the Insert Page dialog box, set the Number of pages and choose Before or After the current page. Click OK.  Deleting pages Delete Page asks which pages to delete: the page number in Delete page (the current page to start with), and to delete a range, Through to page with the last page of it. All of them go in one step, which Undo brings back. A drawing keeps at least one page. Delete Page on a page tab's menu deletes that page at once. Duplicating a page Choose Layout > Duplicate Page, or right-click the page tab and choose Duplicate Page. Under Insert new page, choose Before selected page or After selected page. Choose Copy layer(s) only for a page with the same layers and nothing on them, or Copy layer(s) and their contents to copy the objects too. Click OK. The copy becomes the current page; Edit > Undo removes it. The page tab menu also has Insert Page After, Insert Page Before, Delete Page and Switch Page Orientation. Renaming a page Choose Layout > Rename Page, or double-click the page tab. Type the Page name and click OK.  Page size and orientation Layout > Page Size opens the Page Size dialog box: Type the Width and Height; Swap exchanges them. Tick Apply to all pages to change every page, or leave it off to change the current page only. Click OK.  Switch Page Orientation turns the page between portrait and landscape. With nothing selected, the property bar of the Pick tool also sets the page size and orientation. The full page settings are in Document options. Page numbers Layout > Insert Page Number puts a page number On Active Layer, On All Pages, On All Odd Pages or On All Even Pages. The numbers on master layers show the right number on every page. Object > Insert > Page Number places one in the text you are editing. Layout > Page Number Settings sets how they look: Start at: the first number; Prefix and Suffix: text around the number, such as "Page "; Style: 1, 2, 3, I, II, III, i, ii, iii, A, B, C or a, b, c; Position: Bottom centre, Bottom outer corner, Top centre or Top outer corner.  Page background Layout > Page Background sets the color behind every page; see Document options.

h: The layout Working in multipage view
x: Multipage view View > Multipage View lays every page of the drawing out on the desktop at once, so you can compare pages and edit them side by side. The layout The pages sit in a grid, in page order: two columns for up to four pages, three for up to nine, and so on. Each page shows its number and name below it; the current page's are in the normal text color, the others dimmed. Working in multipage view The current page is edited as usual: rulers, guidelines, grids and the status bar refer to it. Click or drag on another page to make it current and work there at once. The page tabs and the navigator change the current page too. Zoom To Fit (F4) fits every page in the window. Choose Multipage View again to go back to one page at a time. Page Sorter View shows the pages as thumbnails instead; the two views exclude each other.

h: General Page size Layout Background Bleed Rulers Grid Guidelines
x: Document options Layout > Document Options opens the settings of the active drawing: page size, layout, background, bleed, rulers, grid and guidelines. Double-clicking a ruler or the page border also opens it. Choose a page from the list on the left. Changes show at once; OK keeps them and Cancel puts everything back. Save as default keeps the grid, ruler and guideline settings for new drawings. General  Rendering resolution: the resolution of effects that are turned into pixels, such as drop shadows and bitmap effects. Fill open curves (off at first): when on, open curves show their fill as if they were closed. Auto inflate bitmaps for effects (on at first): bitmaps grow to make room for effects that spread past their edges. Duplicate offset: how far Duplicate places the copy. Page size  Choose Page size for a paper size, or Label presets for sheets of labels, which set the page to the sheet size and add guidelines around each label. Size, Width and Height, and Portrait or Landscape. Apply size to current page only: change the current page only. Show page border, and Add Page Frame, which adds a rectangle the size of the page. Rendering resolution, Bleed and Show bleed area (see below). Layout  The page shows how many pages the drawing has, with Page Sorter View and Switch Page Orientation, and lists the Master layers, each shown on All pages, Odd pages or Even pages. The buttons add a new master layer for all, odd or even pages. See Master layers. Background  Choose No background, a Solid color, or a Bitmap (Choose bitmap) to show behind every page. Bleed  Bleed is the part of the drawing that runs past the edge of the page, so the print has no white edge once trimmed. Set the Bleed distance and tick Show bleed area to see it. Printing and PDF export can include the bleed; see Printing. Rulers  Units: the drawing units (inches, millimeters, picas, points, pixels, ciceros, didots, feet, yards, miles, centimeters, meters or kilometers). Drawing scale: makes a distance on the page stand for a distance in the world, such as 1:100. Choose a typical scale, or type the page distance and the world distance. Rulers, positions, sizes and new dimension lines then show world distances; page sizes, outline widths and text sizes do not. Origin: where the rulers count from (Horizontal and Vertical); Reset origin to the page corner puts it back. You can also drag the origin out of the corner where the rulers meet. Tick divisions: the number of ticks between ruler numbers. Nudge: the Nudge distance of the arrow keys (2.54 mm), the Super nudge with Shift (5.08 mm) and the Micro nudge with Ctrl (0.254 mm). Show rulers. Grid  Document grid: Show grid, Snap to grid, the Horizontal and Vertical spacing (10 mm at first), as a distance or as lines per unit, and Show grid as Lines or Dots. Baseline grid: lines across the page for lining up text, with the Baseline grid spacing (14 points), the Start from top (12.7 mm) and the Line color. Pixel grid: the Color and Opacity of the grid of pixels, Show grid at 800% or higher zoom and Snap to pixels. Guidelines  Show guidelines and Snap to guidelines. Default guideline color and Default preset guideline color. Presets: one inch margins, bleed area, page borders, printable area, a three-column newsletter, a basic grid and an upper left grid. User defined: Margins (Top, Bottom, Left, Right), Columns (Number of columns and Distance between) and a Grid (Rows and Columns). Apply Presets adds them; a line that is already there is not added twice. See Rulers, grids and guidelines for working with guidelines on the page.

h: Rulers The document grid Guidelines The Guidelines panel
x: Rulers, grids and guidelines Rulers, grids and guidelines help you place objects precisely. None of them print. Rulers The rulers run along the top and left of the drawing window, in the drawing units; View > Rulers shows or hides them. A dashed line on each ruler follows the pointer. Drag from the corner where the rulers meet to move the origin, the point the rulers count from. Positions on the property bar, the status bar and in the panels count from it too. Drag from a ruler to add a guideline. Double-click a ruler to open its settings; see Document options, where you also set the units and the drawing scale. The document grid View > Grid > Document Grid shows a grid of lines or dots over the page, behind the objects; Document Grid in Snap To makes objects snap to it. Its spacing (10 mm at first) is set in Document options. When lines would be too close, only every second, fifth or tenth line is drawn. The baseline grid (Baseline Grid) draws lines across the page like a ruled notebook, for lining up text; the pixel grid (Pixel Grid) shows the pixels of the drawing in the Pixels view from 800% zoom. Guidelines Guidelines are lines across the drawing window that objects can snap to. Drag from the top ruler for a horizontal guideline, from the left ruler for a vertical one. With the Pick tool, click a guideline to select it (Shift+click adds), and drag it to move it. Drop it outside the drawing window, or press Delete, to delete it. Click the selected guideline again to show its rotation handles, and drag them to turn it. Right-click a guideline to delete, lock or unlock it, or open its properties. Locked guidelines can be selected but not moved or deleted. Edit > Select All > Guidelines selects every guideline of the page, and Guidelines shows or hides them. With guidelines selected (and no objects), Copy and Paste make copies in the same place, and Duplicate makes copies moved by the duplicate offset (set in Layout > Document Options, General). The Transformations panel moves, rotates and scales selected guidelines as it does objects. The Guidelines panel The Guidelines panel places guidelines by their coordinates. Open it from Window > Panels.  Show and Snap turn guidelines on and snapping to them. Choose the Guideline type: horizontal, vertical or angled. Type the position (x, y, and the Angle for an angled one), counted from the ruler origin. Click Add to add a guideline, or select one in the list and click Modify to move it. The list shows the page's guidelines of that type (Ctrl+click to select several). Delete, Lock and Unlock act on the selected ones, and Guideline color and Guideline style (Solid, Dashed, Dotted or Dash dot) change their look. Ready-made sets of guidelines (margins, columns, grids) are on the Guidelines page of the document options.

h: Turning snapping on and off What objects snap to Snapping while moving Dynamic and alignment guides
x: Snapping Snapping pulls the pointer, and the objects you move, onto exact points: nodes, the middles of segments, the centers of shapes, guidelines, the grid or the page. It makes it easy to join lines and line objects up without zooming in. Turning snapping on and off View > Snap To, or the Snap To list on the standard toolbar, turns snapping to Pixels, Document Grid (Ctrl+Y), Baseline Grid, Guidelines, Objects (Alt+Z) and Page on and off. At first objects, guidelines and the page are on. Snap Off (Alt+Q) turns all snapping off and on again. What objects snap to When snapping to objects is on, these points attract the pointer within the snapping radius (10 screen pixels at first). Each shows its mark and, with screen tips on, its name. Node the nodes of outlines, the corners of rectangles, the points of polygons Intersection where two outlines cross Midpoint halfway along each segment Quadrant the top, bottom, left and right of ellipses Tangent where a line you draw touches an ellipse or curve Perpendicular where a line you draw meets a segment at a right angle Edge the nearest point of an outline Center the center of shapes, bitmaps and tables Text baseline the baseline of a line of text Points win over guidelines, guidelines over the grids, and edges come last. The modes, the radius and the marks are set on the Snapping page of the options; see TraceDraw options. Snapping while moving When you start moving a selection with the Pick tool on one of its points (a node, a midpoint or the center), that point is carried onto the other object's point or edge. Otherwise the edges and center of the selection's box snap to guidelines, grids, the page and other objects. The handles snap while you resize. Dynamic and alignment guides View > Dynamic Guides (Alt+Shift+D) shows temporary guides at 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees through the points you pass over, so you can draw along them. Alignment Guides (Alt+Shift+A) shows guides when the object you move lines up with others.

h: Describing the drawing The report
x: Document properties File > Document Properties opens the Document Properties dialog box. It keeps information about the drawing, such as its title and author, and reports everything the drawing holds.  Describing the drawing Language: the language of the drawing's text, or none. PDF files written from the drawing carry it, which helps screen readers. Title, Subject, Author, Copyright, Tags (keywords written to PDF and SVG files) and Notes (several lines). Rating: none or one to five stars. Click OK to keep the changes, as one undo step. Cancel leaves everything as it was. The title, subject and rating can also be set when you save; see Save As. The report Under the fields, a report lists what the drawing holds, in sections: File: the name and location of the file. Document: the pages and layers, the page size (in the drawing units and in pixels), the orientation and the resolution. Color: the color profiles, the primary color mode and the rendering intent. Graphic Objects: the number of objects and of points, the most points and parts one curve has, and the curves, rectangles, ellipses, polygons, groups and tables. Text Statistics: artistic and paragraph texts, characters, words and the fonts used. Bitmap Objects: the number of bitmaps, their total pixels and the largest one. Styles: object and color styles. Effects: each effect, with how many objects use it. Fills and Outlines: the objects by kind of fill and outline, and how many use each color model. Symbols: symbols defined and instances placed. The report helps before sending a file to print: for example, it shows which fonts the drawing needs and whether it holds RGB colors. For a full check, see Preflight.

Mapas de bits Los mapas de bits son imágenes hechas de píxeles, como fotos y escaneos. TraceDraw los coloca en los dibujos, cambia su modo de color y su tamaño, los endereza, enmascara colores, aplica efectos y los vectoriza en formas. También convierte objetos vectoriales en mapas de bits. Para traer una imagen, use Archivo > Importar; vea Importar archivos. Con un mapa de bits seleccionado, la barra de propiedades tiene los comandos de mapa de bits: editar, recortar, vectorizar, enderezar y remuestrear. Para los efectos, vea Efectos de mapa de bits.

t: Convertir objetos en mapas de bits
h: Ajustes
x: Convertir objetos en mapas de bits Mapas de bits > Convertir a mapa de bits (también Objeto > Convertir a mapa de bits) convierte los objetos seleccionados en un único mapa de bits. Úselo para aplanar ilustraciones complejas o para preparar objetos para efectos de mapa de bits. Es un solo paso de deshacer.  Ajustes Resolución: elíjala de la lista (de 72 a 600 ppp) o escriba un valor (de 36 a 2400; 300 de forma predeterminada). Modo de color: Blanco y negro (1 bit), Escala de grises (8 bits), Con paleta (8 bits), Color RGB (24 bits, opción predeterminada) o Color CMYK (32 bits). Tramado: para Blanco y negro y Con paleta, mezcla puntos para sugerir los tonos que faltan. Sobreimprimir siempre el negro: el negro del mapa de bits se imprime sobre los colores de debajo. Suavizado (activado de forma predeterminada): bordes suaves; desactivado da bordes de píxel duros. Fondo transparente (activado de forma predeterminada); desactivado coloca los objetos sobre blanco. El cuadro de diálogo muestra qué tamaño tendrá el mapa de bits, sin comprimir.

t: Cambiar el modo de color de los mapas de bits
h: Blanco y negro Duotono Con paleta Colorear mapas de bits en blanco y negro
x: Cambiar el modo de color de los mapas de bits Mapas de bits > Modo convierte los mapas de bits seleccionados a otro modo de color. Todos los mapas de bits seleccionados cambian en un solo paso de deshacer, y se conserva la transparencia. Los modos con ajustes abren un cuadro de diálogo con vistas previas de antes y después. Blanco y negro (1 bit) solo blanco y negro (vea más abajo) Escala de grises (8 bits) tonos de gris Duotono (8 bits) de una a cuatro tintas (vea más abajo) Paleta (8 bits) como máximo 256 colores (vea más abajo) Color RGB (24 bits) los píxeles tal como están Color Lab (24 bits) color Lab Color CMYK (32 bits) los píxeles tal como están; la gestión del color los convierte en la salida Blanco y negro  Elija el método de conversión: Dibujo lineal: blanco donde el gris está en el umbral o por encima (128 de forma predeterminada), negro en el resto; Ordenado: un patrón regular de puntos; Semitono (opción predeterminada): una trama de puntos redondos, de líneas o cuadrados, con un ángulo (45 grados) y un número de líneas por pulgada (60); Distribución de cardinalidad: una textura de aspecto aleatorio; Jarvis, Stucki y Floyd-Steinberg: difusión de error, los resultados más suaves para fotografías. Intensidad (de 0 a 100, 50 de forma predeterminada) aclara u oscurece el resultado. Duotono  Un duotono imprime una imagen en escala de grises con pocas tintas, lo que da tonos ricos con pocos colores. Elija el tipo: Monotono, Duotono (opción predeterminada), Tritono o Cuadritono, para una a cuatro tintas. Haga clic en una tinta para cambiar su color. Edite su curva: en horizontal está el nivel de gris (el negro a la izquierda), en vertical cuánta tinta se imprime. Arrastre en un espacio vacío para añadir un punto, arrastre un punto para moverlo, y haga doble clic en él o arrástrelo fuera de la cuadrícula para quitarlo. Mostrar todo dibuja también las curvas de las demás tintas. Guardar y Cargar guardan las tintas y las curvas en un archivo. Con paleta  Paleta: Colores uniformes, VGA estándar (16 colores), Adaptable y Optimizada (los propios colores de la imagen, reducidos al número de colores que indique, hasta 256), Escala de grises, Sistema o Personalizada (la paleta del documento). Tramado: Ninguno, Ordenado, Jarvis, Stucki o Floyd-Steinberg, con la intensidad del tramado. La paleta resultante aparece debajo de los ajustes. Colorear mapas de bits en blanco y negro Con solo mapas de bits de dos colores seleccionados, haga clic en un color de la paleta para colorear su fondo, y haga clic con el botón derecho para colorear su primer plano.

t: Remuestrear, enderezar e inflar mapas de bits
h: Remuestrear Enderezar imagen Inflar mapas de bits Otros comandos de mapa de bits
x: Remuestrear, enderezar e inflar mapas de bits Remuestrear Mapas de bits > Volver a muestrear da a los mapas de bits seleccionados un nuevo número de píxeles; su tamaño en la página se mantiene.  Escriba el nuevo tamaño en píxeles, como porcentaje o como la resolución que da a su tamaño en la página. Con Mantener relación de aspecto activado, la altura sigue a la anchura. Elija el método: Suave (fotografías), opción predeterminada; Nítido, algo más definido; Píxeles duros (pixel art): cada píxel sigue siendo un cuadrado de un solo color; Ampliar con detalle: suave, y luego enfocado cuando la imagen crece. Haga clic en Aceptar. El cuadro de diálogo muestra los tamaños original y nuevo y la memoria que ocupa la nueva imagen. Con varios mapas de bits seleccionados, cada uno se escala por el mismo factor. Enderezar imagen Mapas de bits > Enderezar imagen corrige fotografías inclinadas, vistas en ángulo o curvadas por el objetivo.  Use la Cuadrícula (su tamaño y color se pueden ajustar) para alinear la imagen. Ajuste los deslizadores: Corregir distorsión del objetivo (de -100 a 100), Girar imagen (de -15 a 15 grados), Perspectiva vertical y Perspectiva horizontal (de -100 a 100). Los botones de giro dan antes un cuarto de vuelta a la imagen. Con Recortar imagen activado, el resultado se recorta al rectángulo más grande con las proporciones originales; Recortar y remuestrear al tamaño original lo devuelve al número de píxeles original. Sin recortar, las esquinas quedan transparentes. Haga clic en Aceptar. Restablecer devuelve todos los ajustes a su valor inicial. Haga zoom y desplace la vista previa con las herramientas que hay encima. El resultado sustituye los píxeles, así que los efectos del mapa de bits se vuelven permanentes. Inflar mapas de bits Algunos efectos, como los desenfoques, se extienden más allá de los bordes de un mapa de bits. Mapas de bits > Inflar mapa de bits > Inflar mapa de bits automáticamente (activado de forma predeterminada) agranda los mapas de bits lo que necesiten sus efectos, con un margen transparente. Inflar mapa de bits manualmente agranda a mano los mapas de bits seleccionados: para la anchura y la altura, escriba el nuevo tamaño en píxeles o un porcentaje (de 100 a 1000%), con Mantener relación de aspecto. La imagen queda centrada.  Otros comandos de mapa de bits Recortar mapa de bits recorta un mapa de bits con la herramienta Recortar; arrastrar una esquina de un mapa de bits con la herramienta Forma también lo recorta. Editar mapa de bits abre el mapa de bits en otro programa. Quitar fondo con IA hace transparente el fondo de una fotografía. Quitar fondo: Quitar fondo. Romper vínculo y Actualizar desde vínculo actúan sobre mapas de bits vinculados a un archivo. Guardar mapa de bits como guarda un mapa de bits como archivo PNG.

h: Calco rápido El cuadro de diálogo Calcar mapa de bits
x: Calcar mapas de bits El calco convierte un mapa de bits en formas vectoriales que puede editar, cambiar de color y escalar sin perder calidad: un logotipo escaneado, un boceto, una fotografía. Calco rápido Seleccione un mapa de bits y elija Mapas de bits > Vectorización rápida. Usa el ajuste preestablecido elegido en la página Calco de mapas de bits de las opciones globales (Imágenes prediseñadas de forma predeterminada). Repeat Last Trace vuelve a calcar el mapa de bits seleccionado como el último calco, sin el cuadro de diálogo, y Open Last Trace Settings abre el cuadro de diálogo con la configuración del último calco. El menú contextual de un mapa de bits también tiene estos comandos, con Vectorizar línea central y Vectorizar contorno. El cuadro de diálogo Calcar mapa de bits Mapas de bits > Vectorizar contorno y Vectorizar línea central enumeran ajustes preestablecidos; elija uno para abrir el cuadro de diálogo de calco. Calco de contorno rellena las áreas de color con formas: Arte lineal, Logotipo, Logotipo detallado, Clipart, Imagen de baja calidad y Imagen de alta calidad. Calco de línea central sigue las líneas con curvas abiertas: Ilustración técnica y Dibujo de líneas.  El cuadro de diálogo muestra el mapa de bits antes y su calco después, actualizado a medida que cambia los ajustes: los botones de ajustes preestablecidos, arriba; Detalle (de 0 a 100): más detalle conserva áreas más pequeñas; Suavizado (de 0 a 100, 25 de forma predeterminada): curvas más suaves, menos nodos; Suavidad de esquinas (de 0 a 100): esquinas más redondeadas; Blanco y negro, o el número de Colores (de 1 a 256); Eliminar fondo (activado de forma predeterminada): omite el color de fondo; Eliminar imagen original (desactivado de forma predeterminada); Vista previa cuenta las curvas del calco completo. Haga clic en Aceptar para calcar. Las formas se colocan sobre el mapa de bits, primero las más oscuras.

t: Enmascarar colores de los mapas de bits
h: Para enmascarar colores
x: Enmascarar colores de los mapas de bits El panel Máscara de mapa de bits oculta o conserva los píxeles de los colores elegidos en un mapa de bits, por ejemplo para hacer transparente un fondo blanco. Ábralo con Mapas de bits > Máscara de mapa de bits.  Para enmascarar colores Seleccione un mapa de bits. Recoja colores en las diez casillas de color: haga clic en el cuentagotas y luego en colores del mapa de bits; cada uno rellena la casilla seleccionada y la marca; o haga clic en Seleccionar colores del mapa de bits para rellenar las casillas con los diez colores que más usa el mapa de bits. Seleccione una casilla y ajuste su tolerancia (de 0 a 100%): cuánto puede alejarse el color de un píxel del color de la casilla y seguir coincidiendo. Elija Ocultar seleccionados (los píxeles que coinciden se vuelven transparentes) o Mostrar seleccionados (solo quedan los píxeles que coinciden, opción inicial). Haga clic en Aplicar. Guardar máscara y Abrir máscara guardan las casillas en un archivo .msk; Eliminar vacía la casilla seleccionada. Cada mapa de bits cambia en un solo paso de deshacer.

t: Removing the background of a bitmap
h: To remove a background Options Tips
x: Removing the background of a bitmap Bitmaps > Remove Background makes the background of a photo or scan transparent and keeps the subject. It works on this computer and needs no AI service. The property bar of a selected bitmap has the same command.  To remove a background Select one or more bitmaps. Click Bitmaps > Remove Background. The preview shows the bitmap before and after, with a checkerboard where it becomes transparent. Set the options below until the subject stands out cleanly. Click OK. Every selected bitmap changes in one undo step. Options Background TraceDraw learns the background's colors from the edges of the picture (up to four, so a gradient or a two-tone backdrop works). To choose them yourself, click the eyedropper and click the background in a preview; each click adds a color. Click a color swatch to take it out, and Automatic to go back to the learnt colors. Tolerance How far a color may be from the background's and still count as background (0 to 100). Raise it when some backdrop stays; lower it when parts of the subject go. Edge softness Feathers the edge of the subject, in pixels. 0 keeps a hard edge. Contiguous (on at first) Only the background connected to the edges of the picture goes, so a white shirt on a white backdrop keeps its inside. Turn it off to remove every pixel near a background color, for example the holes of a letter or a ring. Remove specks (on at first) Small loose spots left in the background go too. Clean edge colors (on at first) Takes the old background's color out of the half-transparent pixels of the edge, so no light or dark halo shows when the subject goes on another background. Reset puts every option back. Tips It works best on a backdrop that differs from the subject: a studio background, a sky, a product on a plain table. For busy scenes, the AI command Remove Background with AI (see AI) separates subject and scene by their meaning. The result replaces the pixels; effects on the bitmap are made permanent. To fine-tune afterwards, use Masking colors.

Impresión TraceDraw imprime creando un PDF listo para imprimir con las hojas, que el visor de su sistema envía a la impresora. Estas páginas explican el cuadro de diálogo Imprimir y su vista previa, cómo combinar datos en un diseño para imprimir muchas versiones, cómo revisar un dibujo antes de imprimirlo y cómo rematar pancartas con un borde y ojales.

h: General Color Composite Layout Prepress PostScript and issues Print preview Other ways to print
x: Printing a drawing Choose File > Print (Ctrl+P). TraceDraw builds a PDF of the sheets and opens it in your system's viewer, where you choose the printer and print. In the browser version, the PDF is downloaded.  General Destination: the printer, a PDF file or a PostScript file. Orientation: match the layout, portrait or landscape. Print range: the whole document, the current page, a list of pages (such as 1-3, 5, 8-), or the selected objects. The selected objects print alone (nothing else of the page, its master layers or its background), on a page the size of the area they cover: with the sheet set to the page's size the paper is that area, on a fixed sheet they are centred at their size (smaller only when they do not fit, unless Keep page size is ticked), and the layouts repeat that area. Copies, collated as whole sets or not. Print as bitmap: each sheet becomes one picture at the resolution you give. Color Composite prints all colors on each sheet; Separations prints one gray page per ink (cyan, magenta, yellow, black, then each spot ink). Convert spot colors to CMYK prints spot inks as their CMYK mix. Composite Print text in black. Always overprint black: full black fills and outlines print over the colors beneath. Layout As in document, Fit to page, or Scale to a percentage. Fit to page also shrinks objects larger than the page (or the selection, when you print only that) so they print whole on it. Bleed limit: how far beyond the page objects print (4 mm at first). The imposition: several pages on one sheet, or a booklet, whose pages are paired for folding, with the sheet size and the gap between pages. A sketch shows the result. For the back of double-sided cards, tick Back side: the pages run right to left on the sheet, so each one prints behind its front, and the text is not mirrored. Keep page size keeps the pages at their size on a fixed sheet: they do not shrink for the marks, and the columns and rows stay as you set them (pages that do not fit run off the sheet, and a warning says so). Without it, the pages shrink to fit the columns and rows you ask for. In Print Preview, drag on the sheet to move the page information. Prepress Invert and Mirror the whole sheet, for film. Print file information (the drawing's name or your own text, the page numbers, sheet number and date) and Print page numbers. Crop marks (and fold marks for booklets), Registration marks, Color bars and Densitometer scale. PostScript and issues With a PostScript file as the destination, the PostScript tab sets the language level (2 or 3). The Issues tab shows what the preflight check finds; see Preflight. Apply keeps the settings for the next time; see Global options for the defaults. Print preview File > Print Preview, or Print preview in the Print dialog box, shows the sheets exactly as they will print, with the imposition and the marks. The bar at the top has Print, Close, the sheet shown with previous and next (PgUp, PgDn), the plate to show while printing separations, and the zoom. The options on the left change the sheets at once. Other ways to print File > Send To saves a PDF to your desktop or documents folder, or attaches it to an email. Publish to PDF writes a PDF with full control of its settings; see Publishing to PDF.

h: Setting up a merge The Print Merge panel Kinds of field Editing the records
x: Print merge Print merge fills a design with data, to make many versions of it: name badges, numbered tickets, certificates, labels with QR codes. Each record of your data becomes a copy of the page, filled in. Setting up a merge Design the page. Where a value goes, type the field name in angle brackets in a text object, such as <Name>. Choose File > Print Merge > Create/Load Print Merge. Add the data: Import file reads a CSV file (separated by commas, semicolons or tabs, as Excel or any other program saves it) or an Excel workbook (.xlsx, its first sheet) whose first line names the fields. Fields named like a photo or a picture, or whose cells are picture files, start as pictures, fields named QR as QR codes; the types show at once to be changed; or Add column to add fields by hand, then add records with +. Click Finish. The Print Merge panel opens, where you put the fields on the page and make the merge.  The Print Merge panel The Print Merge panel (also under Window > Panels) works with the data source you created or loaded: Create and Edit open the records. Choose the kind of field, Text, Picture or QR code, and the column under Data source columns. For a picture, Pictures folder chooses the folder your photos are in, when the data names only their files (a name without an extension, such as 1024, finds 1024.jpg or 1024.png). Placeholder image chooses a picture that stands in for the merged ones while you design, and Align and scale sets where each picture goes in its frame: click one of the nine points to anchor it, then choose Actual size, Fit proportionally, Fill proportionally (the frame cuts what is outside) or Stretch to fill. Insert Field puts the field in the text you are editing, or places a new text, picture frame or QR square in the middle of the view. Move and size it like any object. To put each photo inside a shape of your own (a circle, an oval, any outline, also inside a grouped card design), choose Image and the photo column, select the shape and click Place Inside Frame. Every card's photo then goes inside that shape, placed by the alignment and scale. Select a field and click Update Field to change its column or its alignment and scale. Create Merged Document makes the merged pages in a new drawing: the page you are on is copied once per record and each copy is filled in. Your design stays as it is. Print Merged Document does the same and opens Print. Perform Merge instead adds the filled copies to the current drawing, right after the page, named after the page and the record number. Kinds of field Text: replaces <Field> in every text of the page. Number: a counter you do not type: a start, a step and a number of digits (start 7, step 3, digits 3 gives 007, 010, 013). Picture: the cell holds the path of a picture. A text holding only <Field> becomes the picture, as large as fits its box. Put that text inside a frame with Place Inside Frame (a photo frame) and the picture fills the frame, cut by it. A rectangle, ellipse or curve named <Field> (in the Objects panel) takes the picture inside it the same way. Fields work in groups and frames too, so a card can be grouped. QR code: a text holding only <Field> becomes a QR code of the cell's text. An empty cell, or a picture that does not load, removes that object from the record's page. Editing the records Configure columns renames fields, changes their type and counter settings, and removes fields. View single record shows one record as a form; use the arrows or Go to record to move through them. The placeholder buttons insert a field into the text you are editing. Save data source writes the records as a CSV file. To work on several cells at once, drag from one cell to another, or over the record numbers or the field names to take whole records or fields. Then Add adds as many empty records after them, Delete removes their records and Clear (or the Delete key) empties the cells. Edit Print Merge reopens the records.

h: The checks Using the list
x: Preflight Preflight checks a drawing for what tends to go wrong in print, before you print it or send it to a print shop. Choose File > Preflight. The Print dialog box also runs the checks and shows how many issues it found.  The checks Empty text object text with nothing in it Text does not fit its frame paragraph text with hidden lines Font not installed text in a font that is not installed Very small text text smaller than 5 points as printed Small text in rich black small black text made of several inks RGB color in a CMYK drawing screen colors in a drawing meant for print Object off the page objects outside the page and its bleed Low-resolution bitmap bitmaps below 200 dpi as placed Very high-resolution bitmap bitmaps above 1200 dpi Very thin outline outlines thinner than 0.1 mm White set to overprint white that would vanish when printed Empty page pages with no objects Objects that will not print objects on hidden or non-printing layers Warnings are likely problems; notes are worth a look. Using the list The top of the box shows the outcome. Each kind of issue has a heading with its count; click it to open or close it. Click an issue to go to its page and select its object. Under the list, the box says what to do about the kind you picked. Check again runs the checks again after you fix things. Choose checks turns checks on and off and sets their limits: the bitmap resolutions, the smallest text sizes and the thinnest outline. Defaults puts them back.

h: Source Border Grommets
x: Border and grommets Tools > Border and Grommet finishes large prints such as banners and canvases: it grows the page by a border and places grommet marks, where the eyelets will be punched, along its edge.  The preview on the left shows the final page, the border band, the original area (dashed) and the grommets, with the final height and width. Source Choose Page, or Selection to make the box of the selected objects the page. Border Tick Add border and choose its type: Mirror the edges: the design is mirrored out into the border; Stretch the edges: the edge pixels are stretched out; Solid color: the border is filled with one color. Set the size (31.75 mm at first), the same on every side. The design stays where it is; mirrored and stretched edges are made from a picture of the design, placed behind it, so your objects stay editable. Grommets Tick Add grommets, then set: Use border area: center each grommet in the border band; Size: the diameter of the grommet (6.35 mm at first); Margin: from the outer edge to the grommet (31.75 mm at first). Under Placement and distribution, choose the edges (corners, top, bottom, left, right; all at first), then the number of grommets per edge (4 at first) or the spacing between them. Corner grommets are shared by the two edges. The grommets are drawn as thin circles on a layer of their own. Reset puts every field back; OK is available when a border or grommets are on.

Gráficos web Los gráficos para páginas web, aplicaciones y pantallas suelen ser mapas de bits (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) a resolución de pantalla, o archivos SVG que se mantienen nítidos a cualquier tamaño. Estas páginas explican cómo exportarlos de uno en uno y cómo exportar muchas páginas y objetos a la vez. Los objetos también pueden llevar enlaces que funcionan en los archivos SVG, HTML y PDF exportados; vea Enlaces y marcadores.

h: Choosing a format Size and resolution Before exporting text
x: Exporting for the web File > Export For > Web opens the Export dialog box set up for screens: PNG at 96 dpi. It keeps its own settings, apart from Export. Office does the same for office documents (PNG at 150 dpi).  Choosing a format PNG: sharp edges and transparency; best for logos, icons and illustrations. JPEG: small files for photos; no transparency. Set the quality (1 to 100). WebP: small files with transparency; set the quality. GIF: few colors, with transparency. SVG: vector graphics that stay sharp at any size and keep links and object names. HTML: a web page with the drawing. Size and resolution For bitmap formats, set the resolution, or type the width or height in pixels: the other side follows the proportions of the page. For a 32 by 32 pixel icon, type 32. With Transparent background on, the empty parts of the page stay transparent in PNG, WebP and GIF files. Selected only exports only the selected objects, cropped to them; All pages exports every page. The preview shows what will be written, and the dialog box estimates the file size. Before exporting text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies text for the web. To export many pages or objects at once, see The Export panel.

h: Adding assets Exporting
x: The Export panel The Export panel keeps a list of assets (pages and objects) and exports them all at once, each in its own format, to one folder: the icons of an app in several sizes, every page of a set of social media posts. Open it from Window > Panels.  Adding assets Add pages adds every page of the drawing, named after the page. Add selection adds the selected objects as one asset, cropped to them, named after the object. New assets take the format and resolution set under New assets (PNG at 150 dpi at first). Each asset has a tick (only ticked assets are exported), its name (the file name), its format, its resolution for bitmap formats (72 to 2400 dpi) and a cross to remove it. The link under the name goes to the page or selects the objects. Exporting Click Browse to choose the folder (the first export asks for one). Click Export. The button shows how many assets will be written. Characters that files cannot have in their name become _, and two assets with the same name get " (2)", " (3)" and so on. The status bar says how many files were written. In the browser, every file is downloaded.

Formatos de archivo TraceDraw guarda su propio formato, .tdraw, que lo conserva todo, y también guarda archivos .cdr. Abre e importa muchos otros formatos y exporta formatos vectoriales, de mapa de bits y de impresión. Estas páginas enumeran los formatos y explican cómo importar, exportar y publicar archivos PDF.

h: Saving Opening and importing Exporting
x: Supported file formats Saving TraceDraw (.tdraw) the native format; keeps everything, including effects, styles, comments and fonts CDR (.cdr) versions 14 to 27 from Save As; keeps pages, layers, shapes, curves, groups, text, bitmaps, fills, outlines and transparency; effects are written as plain objects TraceDraw template (.tdt) from Save as Template Opening and importing TraceDraw (.tdraw, .tdt) everything CDR (.cdr), from the oldest versions to the newest pages, layers, shapes, curves, groups, text, bitmaps, fills, outlines, transparency, embedded fonts, the color profile CMX pages, layers, shapes, fills, outlines, images, clips, text SVG, SVGZ shapes, groups, clips, gradients, images, text PDF, AI paths, images, text, clips, shadings, patterns; password-protected files ask for the password EPS, PS, PRN, older AI files paths, images, text, clips, shadings; one page per printed page DXF lines, polylines, arcs, ellipses, splines, hatches, text, blocks EMF, WMF paths, pens, brushes, text, bitmaps, clips PLT (HPGL) plotter pen strokes PSD, PSB the layers as bitmaps, with opacity, visibility and masks PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP, TIFF bitmaps TXT, RTF, DOCX paragraph text with its formatting Exporting SVG, HTML vector, for the web PDF, AI vector, for print and sharing; PDF/X-1a, X-3 and X-4 EPS, PostScript (.ps), PRN vector, for print DXF, PLT vector, for CAD, plotters and cutters EMF, WMF vector, for office programs PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF bitmap PSD bitmap, one layer per layer of the drawing Scripts can add more formats to importing and exporting; see Scripts.

h: Where imported objects go Notes on some formats
x: Importing files File > Import (Ctrl+I) adds the content of a file to the drawing that is open, on the active layer, as one undo step. Open instead opens a file as a drawing of its own. Both read the formats listed in Supported file formats. Where imported objects go At first, imported objects go where the file has them. To center them in the view instead, change the setting on the File Formats page of the global options; see Global options. Notes on some formats PDF and AI: the Import PDF dialog box asks how to read the text: as editable text, which keeps its fonts when they are installed, or as curves, drawn from the fonts the file embeds so the text looks exactly as it does in the file. Options > File Formats keeps the choice. A protected file asks for its password in the Protected PDF dialog box. EPS and PostScript: each printed page becomes a page. PSD: each layer becomes a bitmap with its opacity, visibility and mask. DXF: drawing units are taken from the file. Text files (TXT, RTF, DOCX): become paragraph text, with bold, italic, sizes and fonts where the file has them. Bitmaps: placed at their resolution; see Bitmaps. When some objects of a file cannot be read, or fonts are missing, a message says so; see Notes after opening. You can also drag files onto the window, or paste from other programs; see Paste Special.

h: To export Format options
x: Exporting File > Export (Ctrl+E) writes the drawing, a page or the selection in another format. The Export dialog box shows a preview on the left and the settings on the right.  To export Choose File > Export. Choose the format. The common ones (JPG, PDF, AI, PNG) are first. Set the format's options (below). Tick Selected only to export only the selection, or All pages to export every page. Click OK and choose where to save. In the browser, the file is downloaded. The dialog box estimates the size of the file. With Do not show filter dialog ticked, the next export goes straight to the file with the same choices. Format options PNG, WebP, GIF resolution (or the size in pixels), transparent background; WebP also quality JPEG resolution, quality (1 to 100) BMP, TIFF, PSD resolution PDF standard (PDF 1.4, PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3 or PDF/X-4), bleed, output condition for PDF/X PDF, AI title and tags SVG, EPS, AI, DXF, HTML, EMF, WMF, PLT, PS, PRN none For bitmap formats you can type the width or height in pixels; the resolution follows. PostScript and PRN files hold every exported page. The starting choices are set on the File Formats page of the global options. Export For has presets for the web and for office documents; see Exporting for the web. For PDF files with bookmarks and security, use Publishing to PDF.

h: General Color Document Objects and prepress Text and fonts Security Issues Opening protected PDF files
x: Publishing to PDF File > Publish to PDF (also on the standard toolbar) writes a PDF file with full control of what goes in: which pages, which PDF standard, document information, bookmarks and password protection.  General File name, with Browse to choose another place. Export range: the current document (every page), every open document, the current page, a list of pages (such as 1-3, 5), or the selection. Page size for a selection: the page of the document, or a page the size of the selected objects. PDF preset: Document Distribution, Web, Prepress (PDF/X-4), PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3, or your own; + saves the current settings as a preset and - deletes one. Compatibility: PDF 1.4, PDF/X-1a:2003, PDF/X-3:2003 or PDF/X-4. PDF/X files are made for print shops. Color For PDF/X, the output condition (FOGRA39 at first); the CMYK profile of the drawing goes into the file. A plain PDF keeps the colors as they are. Document Title, Author, Subject and Keywords, filled in from the drawing's properties; a bookmark for each page (on at first) and show the bookmarks when the file opens. Objects and prepress Flatten transparency at a resolution (300 dpi), for PDF/X-1a and X-3, which do not allow transparency. Bleed (0 to 50 mm) around every page. Text and fonts Text goes into the PDF as real text: in a PDF viewer you can search it, select it and copy it, and it keeps its fill, outline, colors and angle. The fonts go into the file as well, so the text looks the same on any computer. In the Text and fonts group of the Objects tab: Export all text as curves (off at first) writes every text as curves instead: the file has no fonts and its text cannot be searched. The curves follow the letters' own outlines exactly, so they stay smooth at any zoom. Embed fonts in document (on at first) puts the fonts in the file. Turned off, the fonts are only named and the viewer uses its own copy. Embed base 14 fonts also puts Helvetica, Times and Courier in the file; otherwise the viewer's standard fonts draw them. Subset fonts puts in only the letters the file uses, which keeps it small, when a font uses less than the share you set (80 %). PDF/X files always carry their fonts. Some fonts do not allow being put in other files: their text is written as curves, the status bar names them after publishing, and the preflight lists such text beforehand. Security Require a password to open the file, and the password. Restrict printing, copying and changes with a password, and the password, then the permissions: printing (not allowed, low resolution only, allowed), copying, changing the content, adding comments, filling in forms, managing pages and text access for screen readers. Show passwords. PDF/X files cannot be protected. The passwords are never kept. Issues The last tab lists what the preflight check finds; see Preflight. Click OK to write the file. If something is missing, such as a password or a page in the list, the dialog box says so in red. Opening protected PDF files When you open or import a PDF that needs a password, the Protected PDF dialog box asks for it. Type the Password and click OK. A wrong password is refused and you can try again; Cancel leaves the file closed.

Personalizar y automatizar TraceDraw se puede ajustar a su forma de trabajar: opciones del programa y de cada herramienta, el aspecto de la interfaz, atajos de teclado, barras y espacios de trabajo. También puede automatizar el trabajo con scripts, conectar un servicio de IA para dibujar a partir de una descripción y llevar la cuenta del tiempo dedicado a un dibujo. Las opciones están en Herramientas > Opciones: cada elemento abre su propio cuadro de diálogo. Los cambios se ven al momento; Aceptar los conserva y Cancelar lo deja todo como estaba. El botón ? abre la página de esta Ayuda sobre la página de opciones que se muestra.

h: General Visualización Edición Nodos y tiradores Marco de recorte Ajuste Guardar Texto
x: Opciones de TraceDraw Herramientas > Opciones > TraceDraw (Ctrl+J) ajusta cómo funciona el programa. Elija una página de la lista de la izquierda. General  Al iniciar {app}: mostrar la pantalla de bienvenida, empezar un documento nuevo o abrir el último documento editado. Mostrar el cuadro de diálogo Nuevo documento (activado): pedir los ajustes de un dibujo nuevo; vea Crear un dibujo. Mostrar la pantalla de presentación al iniciar (activado). Use hardware acceleration (activado): dibuja la ventana con la tarjeta gráfica elegida al lado (Fastest available al principio); desactivado, con el renderizador por software del equipo. Se aplica en el siguiente inicio. Si la ventana no se abre así, TraceDraw vuelve a iniciarse con el renderizador por software y luego con OpenGL, y conserva el que funcionó. Niveles de deshacer: cuántos pasos puede deshacer (150 de forma predeterminada). Visualización  Colores de prueba: mostrar los colores como se imprimirán. Mostrar información sobre herramientas (activado), Ocultar cuadro delimitador en herramientas de curva y Activar el seguimiento de nodos (desactivado: si se activa, la herramienta Selección puede arrastrar los nodos de una curva seleccionada). Vista previa a pantalla completa: Mostrar borde de página. Acción predeterminada de la rueda del ratón: Zoom (opción predeterminada) o Desplazar. Calibración de reglas: sostenga una regla junto a la pantalla y cambie la Resolución de pantalla hasta que las marcas coincidan, para que el zoom al 100% muestre los tamaños reales. Restablecer vuelve a 96. Edición  Ángulo de restricción: el paso de Ctrl al girar y al dibujar (15 grados de forma predeterminada). Precisión del dibujo: los decimales de la barra de propiedades y de la barra de estado (3 de forma predeterminada). Visibilidad de los objetos inactivos (20% de forma predeterminada) y Doble clic activa el modo de enfoque; vea Modo de enfoque. Nodos y tiradores  Tamaño de nodo: pequeño, mediano o grande. Forma de nodo para los nodos Cúspide, Suave y Simétrico. Mostrar dirección de la curva al editar. Mostrar anillos de redondeo de esquinas en los nodos de curva (herramienta Forma). Colores: el Color principal de los nodos y tiradores seleccionados y el Color secundario. Mostrar nodos no seleccionados con relleno (Ctrl+Mayús+G). Marco de recorte  Centrar automáticamente el contenido nuevo: Cuando el contenido está totalmente fuera del marco (opción predeterminada), Siempre o Nunca. Mostrar líneas en marcos de recorte vacíos (activado). Vea Colocar objetos dentro de un marco. Ajuste  Ajustar a objetos (Alt+Z), Ajustar a página, Encajar en líneas guía, Encajar en cuadrícula, la cuadrícula de línea de base y Ajustar a píxeles. Radio de ajuste (10 píxeles de forma predeterminada). Mostrar marcas de ubicación de ajuste y la Información en pantalla. Modos: los puntos a los que se ajustan los objetos, con Seleccionar todo y Deseleccionar todo. Vea Ajuste. Guardar  Copia de seguridad: Hacer copia del archivo original antes de guardar (activado) conserva el archivo anterior como backup_of_<name>, Copiar en la Misma carpeta que el archivo original o un lugar elegido. Copia de seguridad automática (activado): Hacer copia cada 20 minutos, en una carpeta temporal o en un lugar elegido. Tras un bloqueo se ofrecen las copias; vea Copia de seguridad automática y recuperación. Texto  La página tiene cinco pestañas. Visualización: Incremento de texto con teclado (cuánto agrandan y reducen Ctrl+8 y Ctrl+2 el texto seleccionado, 1 punto), la Fuente predeterminada y el Tamaño predeterminado del texto nuevo, y Mostrar caracteres no imprimibles. Text units pt, mm, cm, in, px… Paragraph Text: Mostrar marcos de texto, Usar separación silábica y los Hyphenation patterns (integrados, o un diccionario de división de su idioma). Fuentes: Show recently used fonts arriba de las listas de fuentes, el Number of recently used fonts (5, hasta 20) y el Font sample size. Spelling: Omitir palabras con números, Omitir palabras en mayúsculas y Add corrections to Autocorrect, para que una palabra corregida en el corrector se corrija al escribir la próxima vez; y los Dictionaries que usa, consulte Diccionarios. Autocorrección: lo que se corrige al escribir; consulte Autocorrección.

x: Opciones de personalización Herramientas > Opciones > Personalización ajusta el aspecto de la interfaz, sus propios atajos de teclado, qué barras se muestran y cómo se comporta la paleta de colores. Apariencia  Centrar cuadros de diálogo: los cuadros de diálogo se abren en el centro de la ventana; desactivado, se abren donde los dejó. Sombras en menús y diálogos (menos sombras ayudan con gráficos más lentos). Iconos de herramientas en color: cada grupo de herramientas recibe un color propio. Tamaño: el tamaño de menús, barras, iconos y paneles, en relación con la escala que su sistema da al monitor (100% de forma predeterminada). Restablecer valor predeterminado vuelve al 100%. El tamaño de la interfaz nunca cambia el tamaño de su dibujo. Crecer con el tamaño del texto del escritorio (ahora {n} %) hace que crezca con el tamaño del texto del escritorio. Color: el Tema (Claro, Claro medio, Oscuro medio, Oscuro o Alto contraste), Usar contraste alto mientras el escritorio tenga un tema de contraste alto activo y el Color del escritorio alrededor de la página. El botón del extremo derecho de la barra de estado alterna entre claro y oscuro. Comandos  La página enumera todos los comandos de los menús, con su atajo, y las teclas de las herramientas. Escriba en Buscar para filtrar la lista. Para dar a un comando su propio atajo: Haga clic en el botón de atajo del comando. Pulse las teclas, por ejemplo Ctrl+Alt+K. Esc deja de esperar. Sus atajos tienen prioridad sobre los integrados: cuando toma una tecla que usa otro comando, la página indica qué comando la ha perdido. Los menús muestran su atajo. La x junto a un atajo lo quita, y restablecer los valores predeterminados los quita todos. Las teclas de herramienta son una letra o Shift y una letra. Vea Atajos de teclado. Barras de comandos  Mostrar estas barras Barra de menús, Estándar, Barra de propiedades, Caja de herramientas, Barra de estado, Paleta de colores, y las barras de herramientas Texto, Zoom y Transformar. Restablecer vuelve a colocar las barras. En Otros: Bloquear barras y Mostrar el menú lateral Contorno en la caja de herramientas. While these pages are open (or with Alt held), drag a button of the Standard or Zoom toolbar to move it, or off the bar to remove it. Drag a command from the Commands page onto one of these bars to add it. Reset on the Command Bars page brings the first buttons back. Paleta de colores  Actualizar automáticamente la paleta del documento y Mostrar la paleta del documento (ambas activadas). Muestras de color: Mostrar casilla "Sin color" (activado), y lo que hace el Botón derecho del ratón: Establecer color del contorno (opción predeterminada) o abrir el Menú contextual. Vea Paletas de colores.

x: Opciones de herramientas Herramientas > Opciones > Herramientas ajusta cómo se comportan las herramientas y qué objetos nuevos dibujan. La mayoría de estos valores también están en la barra de propiedades de cada herramienta. Selección  Cursor en cruz: el puntero es una cruz. Curvas  Suavizado a mano alzada: de 0 a 100 (50 de forma predeterminada).
